sources.title: NGSS 4-PS4-3: Generate and compare multiple solutions that use patterns to transfer information

note.text: You can send a message without words by using a pattern: flashing a light on and off.
A short flash is a dot. A long flash, three times as long, is a dash. That's Morse code.

steps.title: Flash
steps.instruction: Draw the three lines of the flash.

note.text: Light travels fast and far, so a friend across a field can read your flashes, even at night.

steps.title: Message strip
steps.instruction: Trace the strip where we'll write the message.

note.text: Writing the pattern down lets you check it, send it again, or decode it later.

steps.title: Letter O
steps.instruction: Draw three dashes: that's the letter O.

note.text: In Morse code, O is dash, dash, dash. Every letter has its own pattern of dots and dashes.

steps.title: Letter K
steps.instruction: Draw dash, dot, dash: the letter K. Dab the dot.

note.text: K is dash, dot, dash. A longer gap between letters, as long as three dots, shows where one letter ends.

steps.title: Decode
steps.question: O is − − − and K is − · −. What does your strip say?

options.feedback: Yes! Patterns of short and long signals can carry any message, letter by letter.
Read left to right: first − − − (O), then − · − (K).
The second letter has a dot in the middle: − · − is K.
There are only two letters here, made of dashes and one dot: O and K.

steps.title: Compare solutions
steps.question: You need to send a message to a friend across a big, dark field at night. Which way works best?

options.feedback: Yes. Light can be seen from far away in the dark, and the code carries the message.
A whisper won't carry across a big field. A flashing light can be seen from far away.

options.text: Wave a note in the air
options.feedback: Your friend couldn't read it in the dark. Flashes of light show up at night.

options.text: Tap a pattern on the ground
options.feedback: Taps won't carry across a whole field. Light flashes travel much farther.

steps.title: Patterns
steps.question: Why does Morse code leave a longer gap between letters?

options.text: So you can tell where one letter ends and the next begins
options.feedback: Right. Without the gaps, − − − − · − would be hard to split into O and K. The pattern needs to be clear.

options.text: To give the flashlight a rest
options.feedback: The gaps are part of the pattern: they mark where each letter ends.
They do: without them you couldn't tell where one letter stops and the next starts.
The gap isn't padding: it shows where one letter ends.
